turns.doctor_question: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, hi. Thanks for seeing me. Well, what made me come in is that, for the past year or so, I just keep getting pulled off track. The smallest thing pulls me off what I’m doing before I can even stop it. Like a phone buzz, or somebody walking past my office. We just moved into this new commercial space downtown, actually. Great square footage, but it's got all these glass walls. My business partner thought it would look more open and collaborative, but honestly, I see every single shadow moving out there. 

Or, I don't know, even a random thought will just derail me. Like, I'll be looking at a spreadsheet and suddenly I'm thinking about my in-laws. Which, don't get me started, they're coming down next month and my father-in-law is already texting me about renting a boat. He always wants to get a pontoon, but he never offers to pay for the gas. It's ridiculous, the guy made a killing in real estate in the nineties but acts like a twenty-dollar gas can is going to bankrupt him. 

But... yeah, what was I saying? Right, I just get pulled away from my work by every little thing before I can catch myself. It's been happening a lot this past year.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient explicitly states they are easily pulled off track by extraneous stimuli (phone buzz, people walking by) and unrelated thoughts (thinking about in-laws).

turns.doctor_question: Have you had this kind of distractibility since you were a child?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, looking back, it was definitely around when I was a kid, too. I mean, my teachers were always moving my seat because I talked way too much, or I'd just get up and wander around without asking. 

I remember Mrs. Gable in... I think it was eighth grade? She actually moved my desk right next to her filing cabinet to keep an eye on me. Which was a terrible idea, honestly, because I just spent the whole time reading the labels on her folders. She had this one red folder that just said "Priority" and I always wanted to know what was in it. Probably just, like, detention slips or something. I actually ran into her a few years ago at a Home Depot, buying mulch. She looked exactly the same, just a little grayer. She was looking at the cedar chips, but I told her the dyed black mulch holds its color way better if your yard gets full sun. 

But yeah, I was always blurting things out before they even finished asking a question in class. School just wasn't really built for me, which is probably why I ended up leaving in tenth grade to just start working. Best decision I ever made, honestly. You don't need a piece of paper to know how to build a company from the ground up. I started with just me and a buddy doing junk removal out of an old Ford Ranger... wait, did that answer your question? I kind of lost my train of thought there.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient confirms having distractibility since childhood and describes being easily distracted by folder labels instead of paying attention.
symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient states they would frequently get up and wander around the classroom without asking.
symptom_reasoning.S015: The patient explicitly mentions that their teachers moved their seat because they 'talked way too much'.
symptom_reasoning.S016: The patient recalls 'blurting things out before they even finished asking a question in class'.

turns.doctor_question: Do you spend a lot of time worrying about different things most days?
turns.patient_response:
Worrying? No, not really. I don't really sit around and stew on things. If there's a problem, I just fix it or move on. Like, just last Tuesday, our main supplier for corrugated boxes tried to hit us with a fifteen percent price hike out of nowhere. I didn't even stress about it, I just immediately called up this guy I know in Omaha who runs a packaging plant. 

Great guy, actually. I met him at a trade show in Vegas back in, like, 2018? Man, Vegas is wild. We stayed at the Bellagio, and their buffet used to be absolutely top tier, but that time we went, the crab legs were totally rubbery. You can always tell when they just leave them sitting under those heat lamps way too long. My wife loves crab, but she absolutely refuses to eat it unless we’re actually on the coast somewhere. We took an RV up to Maine a couple years ago just for the seafood, actually. Driving an RV is a lot harder than it looks, by the way, especially trying to park a thirty-footer at a Cracker Barrel... 

But, uh, what did you ask me? Oh, right, worrying. Yeah, no, I'm not really a worrier. I just keep moving.

symptom_reasoning.S015: The patient talks excessively, providing a long, rambling, and overly detailed response to a simple question.

turns.doctor_question: Do you often feel physically restless or unable to sit still?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, absolutely. I'm always fidgeting or bouncing my leg. Like, when I'm supposed to sit still, especially during those long family dinners or... oh, I volunteer with the finance committee at our church, and those meetings are brutal. It just feels like there’s a motor running inside me, you know? I just have to move or find something to do with my hands. 

Actually, at the last church meeting, I ended up completely taking apart my ballpoint pen and putting it back together like five times. It was one of those nice metal ones, too, a Pilot G2 Pro. Great pen, honestly, the ink flow is so smooth. I buy them in bulk for the office because the cheap plastic ones always dry out or the caps crack. My business partner, he always chews on the caps of his pens. Drives me insane. I told him he's going to swallow a piece of plastic one day and end up in the ER. 

Speaking of the ER, my youngest son, he's eight, he actually had to go last month because he swallowed a quarter. A whole quarter! Just popped it in his mouth on a dare from his cousin. Kids are unbelievable. The doctor said it would just pass on its own, but my wife was practically having a panic attack the whole time... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, sitting still. Yeah, I just can't do it. I always need to be doing something or moving around.

turns.doctor_question: Before these last year of symptoms, was there any major stressful event or change in your life that seemed to trigger them?
turns.patient_response:
Well, yeah, actually. I mean, I've always been like this, like we talked about, but it's definitely been noticeably harder to manage for, I don't know, about a year and two months now? 

That's right around the time this whole massive conflict with my in-laws started taking over, like, our entire family life. It's just been non-stop drama. My wife's sister, she decided to buy this fixer-upper house right down the street from us, which sounds great in theory, right? Family close by. But she expected me to basically be her free general contractor because I run a business. I told her, look, I do junk removal and logistics, I don't hang drywall. But she got incredibly offended, and then my mother-in-law got involved, and suddenly we're the bad guys because we won't spend our weekends putting up shiplap. 

Shiplap is so overdone anyway, honestly. Every house you see on those home renovation shows has it now. My wife watches those channels constantly. We actually thought about flipping houses once, back before the market got totally crazy. We went to this seminar at a Holiday Inn out by the airport. You know, one of those things where they try to sell you a ten-thousand-dollar coaching package at the end? Total scam. But the coffee they had in the lobby was surprisingly good. Usually hotel coffee tastes like burnt dirt, but this was a really smooth dark roast. I actually asked the guy at the front desk what brand it was, but he had no idea. 

Anyway... wait, what was the question? Oh, right, the stress. Yeah, the in-law thing has just been a huge drain on everything for the last year or so, and it definitely made all this other stuff way harder to deal with.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever had a period lasting several days when you felt unusually energized or overly upbeat, with much less need for sleep than usual?
turns.patient_response:
No, I don't think so. I mean, I'm pretty high-energy most of the time, but not like... unusually upbeat for days on end without sleeping. I definitely need my sleep. If I don't get at least six hours, I'm totally useless the next day. 

Although, honestly, getting decent sleep has been tough lately because we just got this new mattress. It's one of those memory foam ones that comes rolled up in a box, which is wild to me. How do they compress a whole king-size mattress into a box that small? The delivery guy practically threw his back out carrying it up our front steps. We had to wait 48 hours for it to fully expand before we could even sleep on it, which meant we were stuck on the air mattress in the guest room for two nights. Air mattresses are the absolute worst. They always deflate right in the middle, so you wake up folded in half like a taco. I actually tried to patch a hole in an air mattress once with duct tape. Turns out, duct tape does not fix everything, despite what my dad used to say. He used duct tape on the bumper of his old Ford pickup for like three years. It was this hideous silver stripe across the back of a red truck. 

But yeah, anyway, no, I don't have periods where I'm just buzzing for days without sleep. Just my normal level of busy.

turns.doctor_question: On most days, do you feel anxious or on edge?

Not really, no. I wouldn't say I feel anxious or on edge most days. I mean, I'm always moving, always doing something, but it's not an anxious feeling. It's just... I just have a lot of energy, you know?

We were watching this documentary the other night about deep-sea diving, which is fascinating, by the way. The amount of pressure down there is unbelievable. Like when I have to crawl under the deck to check the pipes. We had a pipe freeze last winter and it cracked, water everywhere. I had to army-crawl through the mud with a flashlight in my teeth. Reminded me of when I used to play paintball with my buddies back in my twenties. We used to go out into the woods every weekend. I was actually pretty good at it, very quick on my feet. 

But yeah, no, I'm not walking around feeling on edge or anything. Just, you know, always ready to go.

The owner, this guy named Mike, he had this incredible collection of vintage license plates covering the entire back wall of the garage. He said he'd been collecting them since he was a kid. I guess a boat makes more sense. I've only been on a boat a few times, mostly just fishing on the lake. My buddy has this pontoon boat, and we took it out last 4th of July. We tried to barbecue on it, but the grill tipped over and all the hot dogs fell in the water. The fish probably loved it, though.
